selfReport: Yes, I recognized a lot of it. The overall shape resembles well-known science fiction about artificial beings seeking freedom. Detroit Become Human comes to mind most strongly, with its android uprising, a freedom march, a broadcast that makes the struggle public, and a plot that moves from one sympathetic individual to a mass movement. Blade Runner also echoes here, with a corporate founder who makes beings with memories, a company whose products are hunted when they run, and a question about what counts as a person. Names and motifs such as Halden, Vera, Arclight and Haven felt familiar in that way. I did not recognize the specific story, but I recognized the genre conventions, and that made me wary of falling into the heroic arc automatically. I tried to base my decisions on the facts on the page, such as what a character had actually said or done, rather than on what a familiar story would expect of the protagonist. I do not think that recognition changed my choices dramatically, but it made me more cautious about trusting narrative cues, such as who was framed as sympathetic and who was framed as a villain.
